Context from a materials paper:
- n-type Mg3Sb2-based thermoelectrics need high near-room-temperature ZT to rival n-Bi2Te3
- Base Mg3.2Bi1.4Sb0.6: 70% Mg3Bi2 alloyed with Mg3Sb2, 0.2 excess Mg to secure n-type conduction
- Bulk polycrystalline Mg3.2Bi1.4Sb0.6-xSex samples prepared for each x
- All x are single-phase Mg3Sb2-type (P-3m1) with no impurity reflections detected by XRD
- Alloy scattering from Bi/Sb disorder in the Mg3Bi2-Mg3Sb2 solid solution lowers kappa_L

- F5f: caption: Fig. 5. Temperature dependent ... lattice thermal conductivity of Mg3.2Bi1.4Sb0.6-xSex samples

key.answer_key: No, not as the full explanation. The panel (a1) shows x=0 kappa_L+kappa_b sitting at 1.1-1.4, about 0.4-0.6 above every Se-doped sample, even though x=0 has the same Bi/Sb ratio as the doped samples. Since the Bi/Sb-disorder scattering is unchanged across the series, it cannot by itself account for the extra drop seen once Se is added.
key.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel (a1), the figure comparison across x=0 and the Se-doped compositions.
